question: Which of the following is a national health programme of India for the control of a vector borne disease?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme covers malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — National Programme for Control of Blindness: The blindness control programme deals with eye diseases and cataract surgery

C — National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly: The programme for the elderly deals with the health of older persons

D — National Mental Health Programme: The mental health programme deals with mental illness

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse's role in the vector borne programme is mainly early case detection along with organising source reduction and spraying in the village
option_3: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly

question: Under the National Health Mission the Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Committee is chaired by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. an elected representative of the village panchayat

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The committee is chaired by an elected panchayat member, which keeps the planning of health and nutrition in the hands of the community

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the block medical officer: The block medical officer guides the block level activities

B — the auxiliary nurse midwife: The auxiliary nurse midwife is the secretary or a member of the committee and not its chairperson

D — the district collector: The district collector heads the district health society

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A committee that meets regularly and reviews the services of the sub-centre and anganwadi is one of the strongest supports a community nurse can have
option_3: an elected representative of the village panchayat

question: In the epidemiological triad the organism that causes a disease is called the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. agent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The agent is the organism or the factor whose presence or absence causes the disease, and it is one arm of the triad

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — host: The host is the person or the animal in which the disease develops

B — vector: A vector is an insect or another living carrier that transmits the organism, and it belongs to the environment

D — carrier: A carrier harbours the organism without falling ill and is again not the agent itself

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because the environment is one arm of the triad, the nurse's work on water, sanitation and housing is as much disease prevention as giving medicines

question: The temperature that is maintained in the cold chain for the storage of most vaccines is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. two to eight degrees Celsius

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Most vaccines are kept between two and eight degrees Celsius, which is the range of a domestic refrigerator

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — minus twenty degrees Celsius: A deep freeze is used for the oral polio vaccine stock and for making ice packs, but not for the routine storage of all vaccines

C — fifteen to twenty degrees Celsius: Fifteen to twenty degrees is room temperature and allows the vaccines to lose potency

D — thirty seven degrees Celsius: Body temperature destroys the vaccine in a very short time

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The temperature is checked twice a day and recorded on the chart pasted on the refrigerator, and freeze sensitive vaccines are never kept in the freezer compartment

question: The infant mortality rate is calculated by dividing the number of deaths of children below one year in a year by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. number of live births in the same year

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The infant deaths are related to the live births in the same year and expressed per thousand live births, which shows the risk to a newborn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — number of children below five years: Children below five years form the denominator of a different rate

C — number of women of reproductive age: Women of reproductive age are the denominator of fertility measures

D — total population of the area: Dividing by the total population gives a different and less useful measure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The rate is reported with its two components separately, because neonatal deaths point to delivery and newborn care while later deaths point to the home environment
option_2: number of live births in the same year

question: A family draws drinking water from an open well that lies twenty feet from a cattle shed, and the children have repeated attacks of diarrhoea. The most useful advice is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. remove the animals from the area, protect the well, treat the water by boiling or chlorination and store it in a covered container

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The source must be protected from contamination by animals and surface water, and the water is then treated and stored safely for use

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — allow the water to settle before drinking: Settling removes mud and not the organisms

C — strain the water through a cloth and drink it at once: Straining through cloth removes only the larger particles

D — add sugar to the water to make it safe: Sugar has no effect on the organisms and feeds them

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The well is also disinfected and the rope and bucket used for drawing water are kept off the ground, since the same rope often carries the contamination back into the well
option_1: remove the animals from the area, protect the well, treat the water by boiling or chlorination and store it in a covered container
option_2: allow the water to settle before drinking
option_3: strain the water through a cloth and drink it at once
option_4: add sugar to the water to make it safe

question: Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by the bite of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Culex mosquitoes breeding in flooded paddy fields

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Culex mosquitoes, which breed in paddy fields and other flooded ground, transmit Japanese encephalitis, and the pig and the water bird act as the reservoir

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the common housefly: The housefly carries organisms mechanically and does not transmit this disease

C — the sandfly: The sandfly transmits kala-azar

D — Aedes mosquitoes breeding in clean containers: Aedes transmits dengue and chikungunya

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Control depends on reducing the breeding in the fields and on immunising children in the endemic districts, since the disease can leave severe neurological damage
option_2: Culex mosquitoes breeding in flooded paddy fields

question: A patient with a fracture of the femur is treated in a district hospital after referral from the primary health centre. This is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. secondary care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The district hospital is the first referral level, where specialist opinion and operative treatment are available for patients sent from the primary level

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — primary care: Primary care is the first point of contact in the community

B — tertiary care: Tertiary care is given in medical college and other highly specialised hospitals

D — home care: Home care is given in the patient's own house

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The referral note and the return of the patient with a plan of continued care in the village are what make the referral system work

question: The monthly Village Health and Nutrition Day is conducted at the anganwadi centre by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the auxiliary nurse midwife, with the ASHA and the anganwadi worker

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The auxiliary nurse midwife provides the services, while the ASHA mobilises the families and the anganwadi worker looks after the nutrition and the weighing of children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the village watchman alone: The watchman has no health duty

C — the block development officer: The block development officer is an administrative officer

D — the school teacher alone: The teacher may help with the school children but does not conduct the day

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The day is fixed in the village calendar and announced in advance, since a service that the community does not know about is not used
option_1: the auxiliary nurse midwife, with the ASHA and the anganwadi worker

question: The school health card of a child records:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the height, weight, immunisation received and the findings of the periodic health examination

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The card follows the child through school so that growth and any defect can be seen and treated early

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the family income: The family income is not recorded on it

B — only the marks obtained in the examinations: Academic marks do not belong on the health card

C — the number of days the teacher was absent: The teacher's attendance is an administrative record

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A defect found at one examination and not recorded is often missed at the next, which is why the card is filled in the presence of the child and kept in the school
option_2: only the marks obtained in the examinations
option_3: the number of days the teacher was absent
option_4: the height, weight, immunisation received and the findings of the periodic health examination

question: A 45-year-old man who has worked for years in a stone crushing unit has breathlessness on exertion and his chest radiograph shows small rounded opacities in both upper zones. The most likely diagnosis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. silicosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Inhalation of free silica dust over years produces silicosis, with nodular shadows that are characteristically more marked in the upper zones, and the worker becomes breathless as the disease advances

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — pulmonary tuberculosis: Tuberculosis may occur along with silicosis but produces fever, evening rise of temperature and cavities

C — bronchial asthma: Asthma produces reversible wheeze with an allergic history rather than these shadows

D — pneumonia: Pneumonia is an acute febrile illness with a short history and local signs

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Silicosis has no cure, so the whole effort goes into dust control with exhaust ventilation and water spraying, and into periodic chest radiographs of the workers

question: When an earthquake strikes, the immediate priority of the nurse on duty in a hospital ward is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. protect the patients from injury by moving them away from windows and tall equipment, then evacuate them in order of priority once the shaking stops

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Patients are protected first from falling objects and broken glass, and evacuation follows only after movement stops, in the order of how dependent each patient is

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — shift all the patients to the ground floor immediately during the shaking: Moving patients during the shaking exposes them and the staff to falling debris on the stairs

B — run out of the building at once: Running out leaves the patients helpless and unattended

D — wait for instructions on the telephone: Telephone lines fail during a disaster and the nurse must act on the pre-planned drill

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Every ward has a pre-agreed evacuation plan and a list of the patients who cannot be moved, and it is practised in drills before the event
option_1: shift all the patients to the ground floor immediately during the shaking
option_2: run out of the building at once
option_3: protect the patients from injury by moving them away from windows and tall equipment, then evacuate them in order of priority once the shaking stops

question: The risk factor assessment done under the national programme for non-communicable diseases includes:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. tobacco and alcohol use, physical activity, diet, waist circumference and family history

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The assessment covers the common modifiable and non modifiable risk factors together, since it is their combination that decides the risk

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the type of house and the number of rooms: Housing is part of a general survey and not of this risk assessment

C — only the blood pressure: The blood pressure is only one of the measurements taken

D — only the family history: Family history is important but is not the whole assessment

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The findings are entered in a card that stays with the family, so that the same risk factors can be compared at the next visit
option_1: tobacco and alcohol use, physical activity, diet, waist circumference and family history
option_2: the type of house and the number of rooms

question: Besides conducting the census, the Office of the Registrar General of India is also responsible for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the Sample Registration System

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The same office runs the Sample Registration System, which provides the annual estimates of birth, death and infant mortality rates

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the Integrated Child Development Services: The child development services come under the ministry of women and child development

C — the National Family Health Survey: The family health survey is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with the International Institute for Population Sciences

D — the mid-day meal scheme: The mid-day meal scheme belongs to the education ministry

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because rates are produced by a sample system, they are estimates with a margin of error rather than exact counts, which matters when small villages are compared

question: The most important limitation of a lecture as a method of health education is that it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. allows little two way communication, so the doubts and beliefs of the audience remain unanswered

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A lecture delivers information quickly to many people, but the audience remains passive and misconceptions are neither detected nor corrected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cannot be given to more than five persons: A lecture is in fact suitable for large numbers

B — needs a very large hall: A lecture can be given in any reasonably sized room

C — costs more than any other method: A lecture is among the cheapest methods per person reached

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The limitation is overcome by keeping the talk short and adding questions, group discussion or a demonstration at the end
option_1: cannot be given to more than five persons
option_4: allows little two way communication, so the doubts and beliefs of the audience remain unanswered

question: A 40-year-old man is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis at the health centre. The nurse should inform him that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the diagnosis and the entire course of treatment, including the drugs and the follow-up tests, are free under the national programme

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Diagnosis and the full course of treatment are provided free under the national tuberculosis programme, with a treatment supporter and follow-up to ensure completion

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — he must be admitted to hospital for the whole course: Most patients are treated on an outpatient basis and only the seriously ill are admitted

C — treatment has to be paid for by the patient: Payment by the patient is a common reason for stopping treatment, and it is not required

D — he can stop the drugs once he feels better: Stopping early leads to relapse and to drug resistance, which makes later treatment far more difficult

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also screens the household contacts, since one untreated case at home can infect the whole family
option_1: he must be admitted to hospital for the whole course
option_2: the diagnosis and the entire course of treatment, including the drugs and the follow-up tests, are free under the national programme
option_3: treatment has to be paid for by the patient
option_4: he can stop the drugs once he feels better

question: In an outbreak of cholera in a village, the infected well water that is used by all the families represents which component of the epidemiological triad?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the environment acting as the vehicle of infection

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The water is the environment through which the organism reaches the host, and it is the vehicle of infection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the agent: The agent is Vibrio cholerae, the organism itself

C — the host: The host is the person who becomes infected

D — the treatment: Treatment is part of clinical management and not of the triad

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Breaking the chain at the level of the water source, by disinfection and by providing a safe supply, stops the outbreak far more effectively than treating the individual patients alone
option_1: the environment acting as the vehicle of infection

question: A village tube well stands ten feet from a pit latrine that is full and overflowing, and several families complain of diarrhoea. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. report the matter at once, arrange for the latrine to be emptied and repaired and its site changed, get the water tested and chlorinated, search for cases and teach household water treatment until the source is safe

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Contamination travels from the latrine to the tube well through the soil, so the latrine, the water source and the cases must all be dealt with together

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — do nothing until the next survey: Waiting allows a major outbreak to develop

C — advise them to use only the water from the well of a neighbouring village for ever: A permanent arrangement with another village is not sustainable and does not correct the source

D — advise the families to drink less water: Reducing the intake causes dehydration without removing the infection

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The safe distance between a water source and a latrine depends on the soil and the slope of the land, which is why the site of both is decided together during planning
option_1: report the matter at once, arrange for the latrine to be emptied and repaired and its site changed, get the water tested and chlorinated, search for cases and teach household water treatment until the source is safe
option_3: advise them to use only the water from the well of a neighbouring village for ever
option_4: advise the families to drink less water

question: After the rains, a village reports a sharp rise in the number of persons with fever and chills, and the blood slides of several of them show malarial parasites. The measures the nurse should organise are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. indoor residual spraying, removal of stagnant water and breeding places, use of insecticide treated nets, and prompt diagnosis and full treatment of every case in the village

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An outbreak is controlled by attacking the vector in the adult and the larval stages and by finding and treating every case, since the untreated patient is the source of infection for the mosquitoes

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only the distribution of paracetamol tablets: Paracetamol relieves the fever but does not stop transmission

B — spraying the houses once and taking no other step: A single spraying has only a short-lived effect and must be repeated as per the schedule

C — only the closing of the village pond: Closing one pond leaves the larvae alive in pools, drains and containers

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The blood slides of the fever cases in the whole village are taken during the case search, including the family members of the patients
option_2: spraying the houses once and taking no other step
option_3: only the closing of the village pond
option_4: indoor residual spraying, removal of stagnant water and breeding places, use of insecticide treated nets, and prompt diagnosis and full treatment of every case in the village

question: A district has an infant mortality rate of 60 per 1000 live births and a neonatal mortality rate of 45 per 1000 live births. This pattern shows that the main problem lies in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the care given at the time of birth and in the first month of life

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Three quarters of the infant deaths occur in the first twenty eight days, which points to the quality of delivery care, newborn resuscitation and early newborn care

🔍 Key Clues: infant

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the sanitation of the whole district: Surface sanitation influences later deaths more than the neonatal period

B — immunisation and nutrition in the second half of the first year: Problems in the later months mainly raise the post neonatal part of the rate, which is small here

D — the number of children born in the district: The birth rate does not affect this pattern at all

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The finding directs the programme towards the labour room, skilled attendance at birth and the first days at home, rather than towards the later months alone
option_2: immunisation and nutrition in the second half of the first year
option_3: the care given at the time of birth and in the first month of life
option_4: the number of children born in the district

question: A 60-year-old woman screened at the health and wellness centre has a fasting blood sugar of 118 milligrams per decilitre and a body mass index of 27. The nurse should advise her to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. adopt lifestyle measures such as weight reduction, a modified diet and regular exercise, and to return for a repeat blood sugar test as scheduled

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A fasting value between one hundred and one hundred and twenty five is impaired fasting glucose, and at this stage weight reduction, diet and exercise can prevent the progress to diabetes

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — stop eating rice completely: Removing rice completely is unnecessary and not sustainable; the quantity and the rest of the diet matter more

C — take no action, since the value is normal: The value is above the normal range and needs active management

D — start insulin at once: Insulin is not indicated at this level

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A loss of even five percent of the body weight with regular walking has been shown to reduce the chance of developing diabetes in such persons
option_1: adopt lifestyle measures such as weight reduction, a modified diet and regular exercise, and to return for a repeat blood sugar test as scheduled
option_3: take no action, since the value is normal

question: An earthquake has just occurred and the casualty department receives sixty patients within half an hour. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. carry out triage at the entrance, label the patients by priority, allocate staff and beds accordingly and keep a record of every patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Triage at the entry point, followed by the correct use of the staff, beds and supplies with written records, is what allows the largest number of lives to be saved

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give an injection for pain to everyone and let them wait: Pain relief without assessment hides the signs of internal injury and shock

B — begin treatment with the first patient who arrives: Treating the first arrival wastes time on those who can wait and delays the seriously injured

D — send all the patients to another hospital: Transferring everyone away overloads the receiving hospital and delays care for those who could be treated here

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dead and the dying are separated from those who can be saved, since this difficult decision allows the greatest number to survive
option_1: give an injection for pain to everyone and let them wait
option_2: begin treatment with the first patient who arrives
option_3: carry out triage at the entrance, label the patients by priority, allocate staff and beds accordingly and keep a record of every patient
option_4: send all the patients to another hospital

question: A village school has a high rate of anaemia among adolescent girls although health talks are given every year. The most effective approach for the nurse is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. involve the girls and their families in discussions with pictures and a demonstration, arrange the supply of iron and folic acid tablets at the school and follow up the girls who are anaemic

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Knowledge alone had failed, so the answer lies in active participation plus the tablets and follow-up that turn the knowledge into a cure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — repeat the same talks more often: Repeating a talk that has already failed changes nothing

B — distribute pamphlets in the village: Pamphlets add information without removing the barrier of supply and practice

C — report the school to the authorities: The school has done nothing wrong and reporting destroys the partnership

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The reasons for not taking the tablets, such as stomach pain, the fear of weight gain or plain forgetfulness, are found out and answered, since these are what really decide whether the anaemia is corrected
option_4: involve the girls and their families in discussions with pictures and a demonstration, arrange the supply of iron and folic acid tablets at the school and follow up the girls who are anaemic

question: Dowry and marriage of girls at a very young age are best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. social practices that harm the health and the status of women and girls

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Early marriage leads to early pregnancy with its risks, and dowry leads to harassment, mental stress and even violence, so both are social problems with clear health consequences

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — economic benefits to the family: Dowry imposes a heavy burden on the family of the girl and is not a benefit

B — personal choices with no effect on health: These practices are decided by the family and the community and not by the individual alone

C — purely religious matters: They have social and legal aspects and are not purely religious

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because the decision is made by the family, the nurse works through the community and the local bodies rather than with the girl alone
option_2: personal choices with no effect on health
option_4: social practices that harm the health and the status of women and girls

question: In a village a particular group of families is not allowed to draw water from the common well. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. take the matter up with the village leaders and the local authorities and ensure that a safe water source is available to every family meanwhile

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Denial of access to safe water is a health problem as well as a violation of rights, and it is taken up at the community level while an alternative source is arranged at once

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ask the families to shift to another village: Asking families to move punishes them for someone else's practice

C — ignore the matter, as it is not a health issue: Drinking water is fundamental to health, so the matter cannot be set aside

D — advise the families to use the pond instead: The pond water is unsafe and would cause disease

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records what she has seen and reported, since documented evidence is what allows the authorities to act
option_1: take the matter up with the village leaders and the local authorities and ensure that a safe water source is available to every family meanwhile
option_2: ask the families to shift to another village
option_3: ignore the matter, as it is not a health issue
option_4: advise the families to use the pond instead

question: Rapid urbanisation affects health mainly by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. increasing overcrowding, air pollution, sedentary living and stress, with a rise in non-communicable diseases along with the continuing burden of infections

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cities bring together overcrowded housing, polluted air, traffic, inactivity and mental stress, so the non-communicable diseases rise while tuberculosis, dengue and diarrhoeal disease continue

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — removing the need for health services: Cities in fact need more services, particularly for the poor in slums

C — reducing the number of diseases altogether: Urbanisation changes the pattern of disease and does not reduce it

D — improving the diet of every family: Cheap processed food and lack of time often worsen the diet

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The urban poor carry a double burden, living with the overcrowding of the city and the deprivation of a village, which is why urban health services must reach the slums
option_1: increasing overcrowding, air pollution, sedentary living and stress, with a rise in non-communicable diseases along with the continuing burden of infections

question: In an experiment the variable that the researcher deliberately manipulates is called the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. independent variable

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The independent variable is the one the researcher controls, such as the treatment or the teaching programme given to one group

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — constant: A constant is a value that does not change

B — extraneous variable: An extraneous variable is an unwanted factor that is controlled or measured so that it does not confuse the result

C — dependent variable: The dependent variable is the outcome that is measured and is expected to change

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: In a study on the effect of teaching on hand hygiene, the teaching is the independent variable and the observed practice is the dependent variable

question: A hypothesis in research is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a statement of the expected relationship between two variables, which can be tested

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A hypothesis predicts what the researcher expects to find and is either supported or rejected by the results

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the list of references: References are listed at the end of the report

B — the name of the statistical test used: The test is chosen according to the design and the data

C — the final conclusion of the study: The conclusion is drawn after the data have been analysed

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A clear hypothesis decides what data must be collected, which is why it is written before the study begins and not after the results are known
option_2: the name of the statistical test used
option_4: a statement of the expected relationship between two variables, which can be tested

question: Confidentiality in research means that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the identity of the participants and their personal data are not disclosed to anyone without their permission

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Personal details are kept private and the data are reported in a way that no individual can be identified

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the researcher keeps the data for personal use: Data are used only for the stated purpose of the study

C — the findings are never published: The findings are published, but without identifying information

D — the participants' names are printed along with the results: Naming participants would be a clear breach of confidentiality

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: Coded numbers are used in place of names, and the code list is kept in a locked place, so that even an accidental leak of the data sheet reveals nothing
option_1: the identity of the participants and their personal data are not disclosed to anyone without their permission
option_2: the researcher keeps the data for personal use
option_4: the participants' names are printed along with the results

question: A nurse researcher prepares a complete list of all the patients attending a clinic for the month and then selects every fifth patient for the study. This complete list is called the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. sampling frame

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The complete list from which the sample is drawn is the sampling frame, and it must be accurate and up to date

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pilot sample: A pilot sample is a small group used to test the tool

B — control group: The control group is the comparison group in an experiment

C — study group: The study group consists of those who actually take part

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The frame is the source of the sample, so an incomplete frame, such as a register from which defaulters have been removed, gives a biased study

question: A nurse wants to compare the mean blood pressure of patients in two different wards that have no relation to each other. The appropriate test is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. unpaired t test

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Two unrelated groups with a measurement such as blood pressure are compared by the unpaired t test

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — paired t test: The paired t test is used when the same subjects are measured twice

C — rank correlation: Rank correlation measures association between two variables and not the difference between groups

D — chi square test: The chi square test compares frequencies in categories and not means

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The test is chosen from the design and the type of data, and using the wrong test can either hide a real difference or produce a false one

question: The mean, the median and the mode of a set of data are equal when the distribution is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. symmetrical

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a symmetrical distribution the three measures of central tendency coincide and lie at the centre of the curve

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — skewed to the left: In a left skewed distribution the mean lies below the median

C — entirely in categories: With categorical data only the mode can be worked out in this way

D — skewed to the right: In a right skewed distribution the mean lies above the median

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A large gap between the mean and the median is itself a warning that the data are skewed and that the mean alone would mislead

question: In a research report the section that explains the meaning of the findings and compares them with earlier studies is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. discussion

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The discussion interprets the findings, weighs them against the existing knowledge and states the limitations of the study

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — introduction: The introduction states the problem and the need for the study

C — review of literature: The review presents what was already known before the study

D — methodology: Methodology describes how the study was carried out

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A discussion that does not mention the limitations of the study overstates what can be concluded from it, which is a common fault of student reports

question: Which nutrient is lost in the greatest amount when rice is polished and milled?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. vitamin B1 and other B vitamins

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The B vitamins lie in the outer layers and the germ of the grain, which are removed during milling, which is why beri beri followed the wide use of polished rice

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin D: Vitamin D is not present in rice

B — calcium: Rice is a poor source of calcium and little is lost by milling

C — vitamin C: Rice contains almost no vitamin C to begin with

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Parboiling the paddy before milling drives some of the vitamins into the grain, which is why parboiled rice is nutritionally superior to raw polished rice

question: A 3-year-old child has dry eyes with silvery grey spots on the conjunctiva and cannot see well in dim light. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. give the prescribed vitamin A dose at once and advise a diet with green leafy vegetables, carrot, papaya and milk, and complete the remaining doses as per the schedule

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are the signs of vitamin A deficiency, and a therapeutic dose is given immediately along with dietary advice and the follow-up doses

🔍 Key Clues: 3-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give an antibiotic eye ointment alone: An ointment treats an infection and not a nutritional deficiency

B — advise the mother to keep the child indoors: Keeping the child indoors does not treat the deficiency

C — wait for the next round of vitamin A supplementation: Waiting for the routine round may allow the eye changes to become permanent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Night blindness is the earliest symptom and is completely reversible, while the changes in the conjunctiva and the cornea come later and may leave permanent damage
option_2: advise the mother to keep the child indoors
option_3: wait for the next round of vitamin A supplementation
option_4: give the prescribed vitamin A dose at once and advise a diet with green leafy vegetables, carrot, papaya and milk, and complete the remaining doses as per the schedule

question: A 50-year-old man with a painful, swollen right big toe and a raised serum uric acid asks about his diet. The nurse should advise him to limit:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. red meat, organ meats such as liver and kidney, and alcohol

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These foods are rich in purines and raise the uric acid, and alcohol also reduces its excretion, so all of them are restricted

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — green vegetables and fruit: Vegetables and fruit are low in purines and should be taken freely

B — rice and wheat: Cereals are low in purines and form the base of the diet

D — milk and curd: Milk and curd are low in purines and are in fact recommended

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: A high fluid intake is advised, since it helps the kidney to excrete uric acid and reduces the chance of stones forming
option_3: red meat, organ meats such as liver and kidney, and alcohol

question: Which of the following is the best source of dietary fibre?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. whole grain cereals, pulses, fruit and vegetables with the skin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Fibre comes only from plant foods, and whole grains, pulses and fruit and vegetables with the skin are its richest sources

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — egg and fish: Egg and fish are animal foods and contain no fibre

B — sugar and honey: Sugar and honey are refined and contain none

C — milk and curd: Milk and curd contain no fibre

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Fibre lowers cholesterol, improves the blood sugar and prevents constipation, but it must be increased gradually with enough fluids so that it does not cause bloating
option_4: whole grain cereals, pulses, fruit and vegetables with the skin

question: A 65-year-old man on a salt restricted diet for heart failure complains that the food has become tasteless and he is eating less. The nurse should advise him to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. use lemon, tamarind, onion, garlic, and permitted spices and herbs instead of salt, and take small frequent meals of the prescribed diet

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Substitutes that give flavour without sodium make the diet acceptable, and small frequent meals ensure that the intake is maintained

🔍 Key Clues: 65-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — add a little salt at the table: Adding salt at the table defeats the whole purpose of the restriction

B — stop eating the salt restricted diet altogether: Stopping the diet allows the fluid to accumulate and the heart failure to worsen

D — take a salt substitute containing potassium freely: A potassium based salt substitute may be dangerous, particularly if the patient is on a diuretic or has kidney disease

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The family is also included in the teaching, since food cooked for the whole household decides what the patient actually eats
option_1: add a little salt at the table
option_2: stop eating the salt restricted diet altogether
option_3: use lemon, tamarind, onion, garlic, and permitted spices and herbs instead of salt, and take small frequent meals of the prescribed diet
option_4: take a salt substitute containing potassium freely

question: Which method of food preservation works mainly by removing the water that micro organisms need for growth?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. drying and dehydration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Drying removes the moisture so that bacteria, yeasts and moulds cannot grow, and the food keeps for a long time when stored dry

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — adding vinegar: Vinegar acts by making the food acidic

C — pasteurisation: Pasteurisation works by heat and the food must still be kept cool afterwards

D — adding sugar to make a syrup: Sugar acts by drawing water out of the cells and creating a high osmotic pressure, which is a different mechanism

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The food must be dried thoroughly and stored in an airtight container, since a little moisture encourages moulds and produces toxins

question: One gram of carbohydrate provides approximately:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 4 kilocalories

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One gram of carbohydrate yields about four kilocalories, the same as one gram of protein

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7 kilocalories: Seven kilocalories is the value of one gram of alcohol

B — 9 kilocalories: Nine kilocalories is the value of one gram of fat

C — 2 kilocalories: Two kilocalories is too low for any of the macronutrients

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The diet of a patient is planned from these values, which is why the amount of oil in the diet is reduced first when the energy intake has to be cut

question: Hand washing with soap and water is required:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. before and after every contact with a patient and after handling any contaminated article

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hand hygiene at every patient contact and after handling contaminated material is the single most effective measure for preventing infection in hospital

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only after touching blood: Many organisms are carried in urine, faeces and respiratory secretions, not only in blood

B — only before meals: Hand washing is needed far more often than at mealtimes

C — once at the beginning of the shift: Hands contaminate within minutes of starting work, so one wash at the beginning is of no use

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The five moments for hand hygiene, before touching a patient, before a clean procedure, after body fluid exposure, after touching a patient and after touching the surroundings, cover the whole of patient care
option_3: once at the beginning of the shift
option_4: before and after every contact with a patient and after handling any contaminated article

question: While giving a bed bath the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. ensure privacy, keep the room warm, expose only the part being washed and observe the skin for any change

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Privacy, warmth, exposure of one part at a time and observation of the skin protect the patient's dignity and comfort, and the observation may reveal a pressure sore or a rash

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — use very hot water: Very hot water burns the skin and dries it further

C — expose the whole body at once to save time: Exposing the whole body causes chilling and loss of dignity

D — keep the patient flat throughout: The patient is moved gently as required, and a comfortable position is maintained

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The bath is also the best time to inspect the skin of a bedridden patient at all the pressure points, since the patient may not report a sore himself
option_2: ensure privacy, keep the room warm, expose only the part being washed and observe the skin for any change
option_3: expose the whole body at once to save time

question: In collecting a twenty four hour urine sample the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. ask the patient to pass urine and discard it, then collect all the urine passed for the next twenty four hours including the last sample, and keep the container cool

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The first specimen is discarded so that the collection begins with an empty bladder, and the last specimen is included so that the period is exactly twenty four hours

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — collect only the samples passed during the day shift: Samples passed at night are an important part of the total

B — collect only the first sample of the day: A single specimen cannot show the total excretion over a day

D — keep the container in a warm place: Warmth allows the urine to decompose and the result becomes unreliable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse instructs the patient and the relatives clearly, since an error of one specimen changes the result and the estimate of creatinine clearance
option_1: collect only the samples passed during the day shift
option_2: collect only the first sample of the day
option_3: ask the patient to pass urine and discard it, then collect all the urine passed for the next twenty four hours including the last sample, and keep the container cool
option_4: keep the container in a warm place

question: The correct technique of oropharyngeal suctioning is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. insert the catheter without suction, then apply suction only while withdrawing it and limit each pass to about ten seconds

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Suction on withdrawal removes the secretions without starving the patient of oxygen, and the short pass prevents hypoxia and mucosal injury

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — apply suction while inserting the catheter: Suction while inserting pulls the mucosa into the catheter and injures it

C — suction immediately after a meal: Suctioning soon after a meal causes vomiting and aspiration

D — apply continuous suction for a full minute: Prolonged suction causes hypoxia, bradycardia and mucosal damage

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is given oxygen before and after the procedure, and the heart rate and colour are watched throughout
option_1: insert the catheter without suction, then apply suction only while withdrawing it and limit each pass to about ten seconds
option_4: apply continuous suction for a full minute

question: The most comfortable position for a patient who is breathless is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. sitting upright, leaning slightly forward with the arms supported

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The upright position allows the diaphragm to descend and the chest to expand fully, and supporting the arms fixes the shoulder girdle so that the accessory muscles work better

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — lying flat on the back: Lying flat pushes the diaphragm up and worsens the breathlessness

C — lying prone: Lying prone restricts the movement of the chest wall in most patients

D — lying on the left side: The lateral position does not relieve breathlessness as effectively as sitting up

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Pillows over a table or a cardiac table give the support that patients find most helpful, and the position also reduces the work of breathing
option_1: sitting upright, leaning slightly forward with the arms supported

question: The Glasgow Coma Scale assesses:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. eye opening, verbal response and motor response

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The scale grades three responses and gives a total out of fifteen, which is used to follow the level of consciousness objectively

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the pulse, the blood pressure and the respiration: These are vital signs

C — the temperature, the pulse and the respiration: These are also vital signs and do not assess consciousness

D — the pupils, the reflexes and the power: The pupils and the reflexes are part of the neurological examination but not of this scale

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: A fall of two or more points on the scale is reported at once, since it indicates a change in the brain that needs immediate assessment
option_1: the pulse, the blood pressure and the respiration
option_2: eye opening, verbal response and motor response
option_3: the temperature, the pulse and the respiration
option_4: the pupils, the reflexes and the power

question: A 70-year-old man after prostate surgery has continuous bladder irrigation running through a catheter and the drainage is dark red. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. increase the rate of the irrigation as ordered so that the return is light pink, watch for clots and blockage, and monitor the output and the vital signs

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The rate of irrigation is adjusted to keep the drainage clear, and any clot that blocks the catheter and causes retention with pain must be detected and reported early

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pull out the catheter at once: Removing the catheter during the early period is unsafe and is not the nurse's decision

B — record the loss only at the end of the shift: The output is recorded hourly, since a sudden fall in the return indicates a blockage

C — stop the irrigation: Stopping the irrigation allows the clots to form and block the catheter

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The bladder is not irrigated with force by the nurse, since a clot may be pushed into the urethra and cause further damage
option_2: record the loss only at the end of the shift
option_4: increase the rate of the irrigation as ordered so that the return is light pink, watch for clots and blockage, and monitor the output and the vital signs

question: A 60-year-old woman with diabetes is drowsy and dehydrated with deep rapid breathing and a fruity odour on her breath. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. recognise this as diabetic ketoacidosis, give nothing by mouth, start the prescribed intravenous fluids and insulin and arrange immediate transfer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Deep acidotic breathing with a fruity odour and dehydration is ketoacidosis, which needs intravenous fluids, insulin and close monitoring as an emergency

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her a sweet drink: Giving sugar worsens the hyperglycaemia in this condition

B — give her a sedative to rest: Sedation masks the level of consciousness, which is the most important sign to follow

C — wait for the next blood sugar report: Waiting allows the acidosis and dehydration to deepen

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient may also be drowsy with a low blood sugar, so the glucose is checked at once and the correct treatment given according to the result
option_3: wait for the next blood sugar report
option_4: recognise this as diabetic ketoacidosis, give nothing by mouth, start the prescribed intravenous fluids and insulin and arrange immediate transfer

question: Which set of findings indicates that a surgical wound has become infected?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. increasing pain and redness spreading around the wound with a foul smelling discharge and fever

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Spreading redness with pain, offensive discharge and fever indicates infection and calls for a swab and treatment as prescribed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — mild pain on the first day with a dry suture line: Mild pain on the first day is expected after surgery

C — a clean wound with healthy granulation tissue: Healthy granulation tissue is a sign of normal healing

D — a slight itch over the scar: Itching usually indicates healing

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: The wound is inspected and the findings recorded at every dressing, since the earliest change is often a rise in pain rather than a visible discharge
option_1: increasing pain and redness spreading around the wound with a foul smelling discharge and fever
option_2: mild pain on the first day with a dry suture line
option_3: a clean wound with healthy granulation tissue

question: Which bundle of measures prevents pneumonia in a patient who is being ventilated?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. hand hygiene, keeping the head of the bed raised to about thirty to forty five degrees, daily sedation checks, mouth care and sterile suctioning

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These measures together reduce the entry and the pooling of secretions that lead to infection, and they are applied as a set to every such patient

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — giving an antibiotic daily: A routine antibiotic breeds resistance and is not part of the bundle

C — changing the ventilator tubing every day: Frequent unnecessary changes of tubing increase the risk rather than reduce it

D — keeping the patient flat and giving a sedative: Lying flat greatly increases the risk of aspiration

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Even brief periods of lying flat during nursing care count, which is why the head of the bed is put back up as soon as the procedure is over
option_2: hand hygiene, keeping the head of the bed raised to about thirty to forty five degrees, daily sedation checks, mouth care and sterile suctioning
option_4: keeping the patient flat and giving a sedative

question: When a chest drain is removed the nurse should ask the patient to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. take a deep breath, hold it, and then bear down while the tube is withdrawn, and the site is covered at once with an occlusive dressing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Holding the breath and bearing down raises the pressure in the chest, which prevents air from entering the pleural space, and the dressing keeps the site sealed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — breathe out slowly and cough: Breathing out while the tube is withdrawn allows air to be sucked in

B — lie flat and hold the breath for a few seconds: Lying flat does not prevent the entry of air

D — breathe normally while the tube is pulled out quickly: Normal breathing during a quick withdrawal risks a pneumothorax

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: A chest radiograph is taken after the removal, and the patient is watched for breathlessness and for any bubbling at the site
option_2: lie flat and hold the breath for a few seconds
option_3: take a deep breath, hold it, and then bear down while the tube is withdrawn, and the site is covered at once with an occlusive dressing
option_4: breathe normally while the tube is pulled out quickly

question: The expected duration of pregnancy from the first day of the last menstrual period is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 280 days

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pregnancy lasts about two hundred and eighty days, or forty weeks, from the first day of the last menstrual period

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 365 days: A year is longer than a normal pregnancy

B — 210 days: Two hundred and ten days would be a preterm birth

D — 180 days: One hundred and eighty days is far too short for a viable pregnancy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The expected date of delivery is worked out by adding nine months and seven days to the first day of the last period, and it is checked against the ultrasound report

question: Which of the following is plotted on a partograph during labour?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the fetal heart rate, the dilatation of the cervix, the descent of the head, the contractions, the maternal pulse and blood pressure and the urine output

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The partograph plots all these observations together on a time scale, so that a labour that is progressing too slowly is recognised early

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the mother's weight only: The weight is not a part of the partograph

C — the mother's blood group: The blood group is recorded in the case sheet for a possible transfusion and is not plotted

D — the baby's weight: The baby's weight is known only after birth

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: An alert line that the cervical dilatation crosses calls for review and a decision about referral, which is the main value of the chart
option_2: the fetal heart rate, the dilatation of the cervix, the descent of the head, the contractions, the maternal pulse and blood pressure and the urine output

question: A woman has a second degree perineal tear after a normal delivery and there is moderate bleeding from it. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. apply pressure over the tear to control the bleeding, arrange for suturing under aseptic conditions and give the prescribed tetanus prophylaxis and antibiotic

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pressure controls the bleeding temporarily, and prompt suturing with aseptic technique prevents further loss, infection and later problems

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — leave the tear open to heal on its own: An unsutured second degree tear causes infection and poor healing

B — pack the vagina tightly with cotton and leave it in place: A tight pack left in place hides the bleeding and becomes a source of infection

C — ask her to walk to the theatre: Walking increases the bleeding and is unsafe while it is uncontrolled

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The perineum is kept clean and dry afterwards and the woman is taught to clean from front to back, since the proximity of the anus is what makes the wound prone to infection
option_1: leave the tear open to heal on its own
option_2: pack the vagina tightly with cotton and leave it in place
option_3: ask her to walk to the theatre
option_4: apply pressure over the tear to control the bleeding, arrange for suturing under aseptic conditions and give the prescribed tetanus prophylaxis and antibiotic

question: The Apgar score of a newborn is assessed:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. at one minute and again at five minutes after birth, using five signs

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The score is recorded at one and five minutes, and it grades the heart rate, the breathing effort, the muscle tone, the reflex response and the colour

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — at birth and then only once the baby is discharged: The early scores are what call for action, and the later ones show the response

B — only when the baby becomes ill: The assessment is done for every newborn and not only for the sick

C — once, after one hour of birth: One hour is far too late to guide resuscitation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The score at one minute shows the condition at birth and is not used to decide whether to resuscitate, since resuscitation begins on the basis of the breathing and the heart rate alone
option_1: at birth and then only once the baby is discharged
option_4: at one minute and again at five minutes after birth, using five signs

question: A child is said to show failure to thrive when there is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. inadequate gain in weight over a period, as shown by the growth chart

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The growth chart shows the trend, and a flattening or a fall of the curve over weeks indicates that the child is not thriving

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a large appetite with normal weight gain: A good appetite with normal gain is a healthy picture

C — a height above the expected for the age: Being taller than expected is not a failure to thrive

D — a single low weight reading: One reading may be affected by recent illness or inaccurate weighing

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The cause is looked for in feeding, infection, the family's circumstances and, if needed, in medical conditions, since the weight is only a signal and not the diagnosis
option_1: inadequate gain in weight over a period, as shown by the growth chart
option_2: a large appetite with normal weight gain
option_3: a height above the expected for the age

question: A 5-year-old child has a temperature of 39.8 degrees Celsius and has had a convulsion lasting two minutes, and is now drowsy. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. keep the child in a safe lateral position, lower the temperature with the prescribed antipyretic and tepid sponging, protect the airway, monitor the vital signs and arrange assessment for the cause of the fever

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The airway is protected, the temperature is brought down safely and the child is assessed for the underlying cause, since a convulsion with fever may be due to meningitis or another infection

🔍 Key Clues: 5-year-old | 39.8 degrees Celsius

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a sedative and let the child sleep: Sedation hides the level of consciousness and the signs of a serious infection

B — give a cold bath to bring the temperature down quickly: A cold bath causes shivering, which raises the temperature further

D — ask the parents to take the child home and return if the fit happens again: Sending the child home without assessment risks a missed meningitis

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: After the fit the child is kept under observation, and the parents are taught what to do and when to return, since the fear of the episode is often greater than the illness itself
option_1: give a sedative and let the child sleep
option_2: give a cold bath to bring the temperature down quickly
option_3: keep the child in a safe lateral position, lower the temperature with the prescribed antipyretic and tepid sponging, protect the airway, monitor the vital signs and arrange assessment for the cause of the fever
option_4: ask the parents to take the child home and return if the fit happens again

question: The correct method of weighing an infant is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. use a calibrated infant weighing scale with the infant naked, and record the weight accurately to the nearest ten grams

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A naked infant on a calibrated scale gives the true weight, which is then plotted on the growth chart and compared with the earlier readings

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — weigh the infant with the clothes and a wet nappy on: Clothes and a wet nappy add a variable weight that cannot be interpreted

B — weigh the infant only once in six months: Monthly weighing is needed to detect a faltering trend early

C — use the adult scale with the mother holding the infant: The difference between two adult readings on an adult scale is too inaccurate for an infant

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The same scale is used at each visit, since a change of scale makes a small difference in weight impossible to judge
option_1: weigh the infant with the clothes and a wet nappy on
option_2: weigh the infant only once in six months
option_3: use the adult scale with the mother holding the infant
option_4: use a calibrated infant weighing scale with the infant naked, and record the weight accurately to the nearest ten grams

question: A patient with cancer pain is prescribed morphine and the nurse also gives the prescribed laxative because morphine:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. slows the movement of the bowel and causes constipation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Morphine reduces the propulsive movement of the bowel and increases the tone of the sphincters, so constipation is an almost invariable effect and is prevented rather than treated

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — causes vomiting in every patient: Nausea may occur but not in every patient and it usually settles

B — increases the appetite: Appetite is not increased in a predictable way

C — causes diarrhoea: Diarrhoea is not an effect of morphine

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: A laxative is started at the same time as the morphine, since constipation is easier to prevent than to relieve once it has set in
option_4: slows the movement of the bowel and causes constipation

question: A 68-year-old patient on digoxin has a pulse of 48 per minute and complains of nausea and of seeing yellow haloes around lights. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. withhold the digoxin, report at once, record the pulse and the symptoms, and arrange for the blood level to be estimated

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A slow pulse with nausea and disturbed colour vision is the classic picture of digoxin toxicity, and the drug is withheld and reported immediately

🔍 Key Clues: 68-year-old | 48 per minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a double dose to control the symptoms: A double dose may be fatal

B — give the next dose as ordered: Giving the drug increases the toxicity and can cause a dangerous arrhythmia

C — disregard the symptoms, as they are due to age: These symptoms in a patient on digoxin are never attributed to age alone

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The pulse is counted for a full minute before every dose, and the drug is withheld and reported if the rate falls below the level set by the doctor
option_1: give a double dose to control the symptoms
option_3: disregard the symptoms, as they are due to age
option_4: withhold the digoxin, report at once, record the pulse and the symptoms, and arrange for the blood level to be estimated

question: The drug given to reverse the effect of heparin is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. protamine sulphate

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Protamine sulphate combines with heparin and neutralises it, and it is given slowly by the intravenous route in a bleeding patient

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — calcium gluconate: Calcium gluconate is used in hyperkalaemia and in some poisonings

B — atropine: Atropine is used for organophosphate poisoning and for a slow pulse

C — vitamin K: Vitamin K reverses the effect of warfarin and not of heparin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Protamine is given slowly because a rapid injection can itself cause a fall in blood pressure and difficulty in breathing

question: Most of the digested nutrients are absorbed in the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. small intestine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The small intestine has a very large surface with its villi and microvilli, where sugars, amino acids, fats, vitamins and minerals are absorbed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — oesophagus: The oesophagus only conducts the food to the stomach

C — rectum: The rectum stores the faeces until they are passed

D — stomach: The stomach absorbs only a few substances such as alcohol and some drugs

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The loss of a large part of the small intestine leads to serious malabsorption, so such patients need long term nutritional support

question: A 34-year-old man with a spinal cord injury at the level of the neck suddenly has a blood pressure of 180/110 mm Hg with a throbbing headache and a slow pulse. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. raise the head of the bed, check the bladder and the bowel for distension or a blocked catheter and remove the stimulus, and report the episode at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This is autonomic dysreflexia, in which a full bladder or a loaded bowel sends a massive sympathetic discharge, and removing the stimulus is the treatment

🔍 Key Clues: 34-year-old | 110 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a painkiller and wait: A painkiller alone does nothing and the pressure may rise further

B — lie him flat to improve the blood flow: Lying flat raises the pressure even more and may cause a seizure or a stroke

D — give him a hot drink to settle him: A hot drink makes no difference to the stimulus and the situation is urgent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The blood pressure is checked at every catheter change and before any procedure in such a patient, since the trigger is often the procedure itself
option_2: lie him flat to improve the blood flow
option_3: raise the head of the bed, check the bladder and the bowel for distension or a blocked catheter and remove the stimulus, and report the episode at once
option_4: give him a hot drink to settle him

question: The nerve that supplies the diaphragm and controls its movement is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. phrenic nerve

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The phrenic nerve arises from the cervical segments and supplies the diaphragm, which provides most of the movement of quiet breathing

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — sciatic nerve: The sciatic nerve supplies the lower limb

C — vagus nerve: The vagus nerve supplies many organs and controls the heart rate and the secretions

D — facial nerve: The facial nerve supplies the muscles of the face

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: An injury above the level of the phrenic nerve origin paralyses the diaphragm and the patient needs ventilatory support, which is why the level of a spinal injury is so important

question: A 30-year-old woman who is very thin insists that she is too fat and eats very little. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. accept her feelings without arguing, monitor the intake and the weight, offer small frequent meals, and involve the family and the team in the plan of care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The distorted body image is part of the illness, so arguing about it is useless, while a regular plan of intake, weight monitoring and team support restores nutrition and trust

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — argue with her about her weight: Arguments confirm her belief that others do not understand her

C — allow her to decide her own diet entirely: Complete freedom of choice allows the illness to continue

D — tell her that her appearance is frightening: Critical remarks about appearance increase her distress and can worsen the restriction

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The weight is taken at the same time each day with the same clothing, and the nurse stays with the patient at meals, since the fear of eating is greatest when she is alone
option_2: accept her feelings without arguing, monitor the intake and the weight, offer small frequent meals, and involve the family and the team in the plan of care
option_3: allow her to decide her own diet entirely
option_4: tell her that her appearance is frightening

question: The main danger of taking benzodiazepines for a long period is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. sedation, poor coordination and dependence, with distressing withdrawal symptoms on stopping

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Long term use brings drowsiness, unsteady gait, falls in the elderly and both psychological and physical dependence, so they are stopped gradually

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — high fever: Fever is not an effect of these drugs

B — a rise in the blood pressure: These drugs do not raise the blood pressure

D — loss of hearing: Hearing is not affected by them

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dose is reduced slowly over weeks under supervision, because abrupt withdrawal can produce anxiety, sleeplessness, tremors and even convulsions
option_3: sedation, poor coordination and dependence, with distressing withdrawal symptoms on stopping

question: The organism of tetanus usually enters the body through:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a wound contaminated with soil, dust or manure in which the spores are present

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The spores of Clostridium tetani lie in the soil and enter through a punctured or deep wound, where they germinate in the absence of oxygen

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the bite of a mosquito: No insect transmits tetanus

C — inhaling droplets from a patient: The disease is not spread from person to person

D — drinking contaminated water: Tetanus is not water borne

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Every deep or dirty wound is cleaned, debrided and given a booster of tetanus toxoid, since the disease, once established, is far harder to treat than to prevent
option_1: a wound contaminated with soil, dust or manure in which the spores are present

question: The type of anaemia that develops as a result of long continued loss of small amounts of blood is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. iron deficiency anaemia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Chronic blood loss empties the iron stores, and the red cells that are formed are small and pale, which is the picture of iron deficiency anaemia

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin B12 deficiency anaemia: Vitamin B12 deficiency produces large red cells and is due to a lack of the vitamin or of intrinsic factor

B — sickle cell anaemia: Sickle cell anaemia is an inherited disorder of haemoglobin

D — aplastic anaemia: Aplastic anaemia results from failure of the marrow

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A man with iron deficiency anaemia is investigated for bleeding from the bowel, and a woman is assessed for menstrual loss, since the anaemia is only a sign of the underlying cause

question: The purpose of keeping a nursing record is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. provide continuity of care and serve as a legal document of the care that was given

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The record tells every member of the team what has been done and what is to be done, and it is the legal proof of the care given

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — replace the doctor's notes: Nursing records and medical notes are separate and complementary

B — fill the time of the staff: It is not an activity to fill time

D — find fault with individual nurses: The record exists for care and not for blaming

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Entries are made at once, signed legibly, and never altered, since an incomplete or corrected record is a serious difficulty in any legal inquiry
option_3: provide continuity of care and serve as a legal document of the care that was given

question: The enzyme that breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen within the cell is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. catalase
