🧠 Clinical Rationale: Catalase protects the cell from the damaging effects of hydrogen peroxide by converting it into water and oxygen

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — amylase: Amylase breaks down starch into sugars

C — lipase: Lipase breaks down fats

D — pepsin: Pepsin digests protein in the stomach

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Hydrogen peroxide is used to clean a dirty wound precisely because catalase in the tissue makes it froth and release oxygen, which also helps to loosen the debris

question: World Population Day is observed every year on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 11 July

🧠 Clinical Rationale: World Population Day is observed on the eleventh of July to draw attention to population issues and to family planning

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1 December: The first of December is World AIDS Day

B — 24 March: The twenty fourth of March is World Tuberculosis Day

D — 10 September: The tenth of September is observed as World Suicide Prevention Day

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The day is used to talk about spacing of births, nutrition of mothers and children, and the health of the adolescent group

question: The Janani Suraksha Yojana provides:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. cash assistance to poor pregnant women to promote delivery in a health facility

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The scheme gives cash assistance to the mother and to the ASHA to encourage institutional delivery and to meet the cost of transport

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a pension to elderly persons: Old age pensions come under a social security scheme

B — free spectacles to school children: Spectacles are supplied under the school health programme

D — free education to the children of poor families: Education is covered by a different scheme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The payment is made after the delivery and the immunisation of the baby, which also gives the nurse a chance to reinforce breastfeeding and family planning advice
option_3: cash assistance to poor pregnant women to promote delivery in a health facility
option_4: free education to the children of poor families

question: The Pulse Polio programme is conducted in order to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. immunise every child below five years against poliomyelitis on the same day

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Doses are given to all children below five years on the same day across the country, which stops the circulation of the wild virus

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — provide vitamin A to children: Vitamin A is given during the routine immunisation schedule

B — treat children with fever: Fever is treated in the outpatient department

D — screen children for anaemia: Anaemia screening is part of the school health service

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The vaccine is given even to children who have already received it, because the extra doses build the immunity of the whole community
option_3: immunise every child below five years against poliomyelitis on the same day

question: The services of the Integrated Child Development Services are provided through:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the anganwadi centre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The anganwadi is the village level centre where supplementary nutrition, pre-school education and health check-ups are provided to children and mothers

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a mobile clinic only: Mobile clinics are supplementary and not the main channel of this scheme

C — the district hospital: The district hospital provides referral care

D — the medical college: The medical college provides tertiary care

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The anganwadi worker and the ASHA work together in the same village, which is why the nurse coordinates with both for immunisation and nutrition activities

question: The Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram provides for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. screening of children for defects at birth, diseases, deficiencies and developmental delay with referral for treatment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme covers four groups of conditions, and children who need treatment are referred and given free care up to a certain level

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — treatment of adults with chronic disease: Adult chronic disease care is covered by the non-communicable disease programme

B — pensions to widows: Widow pensions belong to social security

C — free travel to pregnant women: Travel assistance for pregnant women comes under a maternity scheme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The school teacher and the anganwadi worker carry out the first screening and the nurse verifies the findings, since many defects are missed unless the child is examined systematically
option_4: screening of children for defects at birth, diseases, deficiencies and developmental delay with referral for treatment

question: As per the Census of 2011 the total population of India was about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 121 crore

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Census of 2011 recorded a population of about one hundred and twenty one crore, which was an increase of about seventeen and a half percent over 2001

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 150 crore: One hundred and fifty crore is well above the actual figure

C — 100 crore: One hundred crore was the population in the Census of 2001

D — 75 crore: Seventy five crore was the population around 1981

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The population figures decide the number of sub-centres, the vaccine requirement and the staffing of each health facility, so the nurse uses the village figures rather than the national ones

question: The National Sample Survey Office functions under the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The office is part of the statistics ministry, which conducts the large socio economic sample surveys of the country

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Ministry of Education: The education ministry has no role in these surveys

C — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: The health ministry conducts health surveys such as the National Family Health Survey with other agencies

D — Ministry of Home Affairs: The home ministry administers the Registrar General's office

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The data on out of pocket spending on health from such surveys show how much illness actually costs a family, which guides the nurse's advice on where free treatment is available

question: The National Health Accounts give an estimate of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the total expenditure on health in the country and the share of each source

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The accounts work out how much is spent on health in total and how the burden is shared between the government, the insurance system and the households

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the number of patients treated every year: The number of patients treated does not appear in the expenditure analysis

C — the number of hospitals in each state: The number of hospitals is a facility count

D — the number of doctors in the country: The number of doctors is a manpower figure and not an expenditure estimate

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A high share paid out of the family's own pocket is what drives families into debt because of illness, which is the reason for the emphasis on publicly funded care
option_1: the total expenditure on health in the country and the share of each source
option_2: the number of patients treated every year
option_3: the number of hospitals in each state
option_4: the number of doctors in the country

question: Insulin is produced by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. pancreas

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas produce insulin, which lowers the blood glucose

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — adrenal gland: The adrenal gland produces cortisol and adrenaline

B — kidney: The kidney filters blood and does not produce insulin

C — liver: The liver stores glucose as glycogen but does not produce insulin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: In type 1 diabetes the insulin producing cells are destroyed, which is why insulin must be given by injection, since it would be digested if taken by mouth

question: The blood group known as the universal donor is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. O negative

🧠 Clinical Rationale: O negative red cells carry neither the A, the B nor the RhD antigen, so they can be given to a patient of any group in an emergency

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — AB positive: AB positive is the universal recipient and not the donor

C — A positive: A positive blood cannot be given to a group B or O patient

D — B negative: B negative can be given only to a few groups

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Only the red cells of O negative are universal; the plasma of AB is the universal plasma donor, as it contains no antibodies against A or B

question: The normal haemoglobin level in an adult male is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 13 to 17 grams per decilitre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An adult man normally has about thirteen to seventeen grams of haemoglobin per decilitre of blood

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7 to 9 grams per decilitre: Seven to nine grams indicates moderate anaemia

C — 4 to 6 grams per decilitre: Four to six grams is severe anaemia needing transfusion

D — 18 to 22 grams per decilitre: A value above eighteen grams suggests polycythaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The normal range for a woman is lower than that for a man, so the same figure does not mean the same thing in both

question: The blood cells that help in the clotting of blood are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. platelets

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Platelets, or thrombocytes, clump together and release substances that start the chain of reactions forming the clot

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — plasma cells: Plasma cells produce antibodies and are not a separate type of blood cell

B — white blood cells: White cells defend the body against infection

D — red blood cells: Red cells carry oxygen and take no part in clotting

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A low platelet count causes bleeding and is seen in dengue and other conditions, which is why the count is watched closely in a patient with a bleeding tendency

question: The immunity that a baby receives from the mother through breast milk is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. natural passive immunity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The antibodies in the colostrum and the milk are ready made and are transferred to the baby directly, which is natural passive immunity

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — artificial passive immunity: Artificial passive immunity follows the injection of ready made antibodies such as antitetanus serum

C — natural active immunity: Active immunity follows an infection and the body makes its own antibodies

D — artificial active immunity: Artificial active immunity follows vaccination

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Passive immunity lasts only a few months, so the baby still needs the immunisation schedule, which is why breastfeeding does not replace vaccination

question: The blood group known as the universal recipient is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. AB positive

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A person with AB positive blood has neither anti A nor anti B antibodies and also carries the Rh antigen, so red cells of any group can be given

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — B positive: B positive blood has anti A antibodies and cannot receive a group A unit

B — A negative: A negative blood has anti B antibodies and cannot receive a group B unit

C — O negative: O negative is the universal donor and not the recipient

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: In practice the same group and Rh type is always preferred, since the universal labels are used only in an emergency

question: For a patient on long term oral anticoagulant treatment, the international normalised ratio is usually maintained between:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 2 and 3

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A ratio of about two to three gives protection against clots while keeping the risk of bleeding acceptable

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 8 and 10: A ratio of eight to ten would be extremely dangerous

C — 0.5 and 1: A ratio of about one is the normal value for a person who is not on treatment

D — 5 and 8: A ratio between five and eight carries a high risk of bleeding

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is also taught to keep his diet steady and to report bleeding gums, black stools or unusual bruising at once

question: The most specific blood test for recent damage to the heart muscle is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. troponin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Troponin is released from the damaged heart muscle, rises within a few hours and stays raised for several days, which makes it both sensitive and specific

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the blood urea: The blood urea shows kidney function

C — the erythrocyte sedimentation rate: The sedimentation rate is a general measure of inflammation

D — the total white cell count: The white cell count rises in many infections and is not specific for heart damage

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The sample is taken as soon as the patient arrives and repeated after a few hours, since a single early normal value does not exclude a heart attack

question: The value of 25 percent of 200 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 50

🧠 Method: One quarter of two hundred is fifty, since twenty five percent is one quarter

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 100: One hundred is one half of two hundred

C — 75: Seventy five is thirty seven and a half percent

D — 25: Twenty five is twelve and a half percent of two hundred

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: A quarter, a half and a tenth are the fractions used most often in practice, and recognising them makes such calculations quick when a stock of medicine has to be shared out

question: A nurse earns 25,000 rupees a month and spends 20 percent of it on rent. The amount spent on rent is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 5000 rupees

🧠 Method: Ten percent of twenty five thousand is two thousand five hundred, so twenty percent is five thousand

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 7500 rupees: Seven thousand five hundred is thirty percent

C — 500 rupees: Five hundred is two percent

D — 2500 rupees: Two thousand five hundred is only ten percent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working out a proportion of a known amount quickly is useful when a family has to be advised about the share of income that treatment will take

question: If 5 injections cost 250 rupees, the cost of 8 injections at the same rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 400 rupees

🧠 Method: One injection costs fifty rupees, so eight injections cost four hundred rupees

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 500 rupees: Five hundred rupees would be the cost of ten injections

C — 450 rupees: Four hundred and fifty rupees would be the cost of nine injections

D — 320 rupees: Three hundred and twenty rupees would be the cost of six and a half injections

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Knowing the cost of a single dose helps a family to compare the price of two packs of the same medicine

question: A stock of 500 tablets is used at the rate of 25 tablets a day. The stock will last for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 20 days

🧠 Method: Five hundred divided by twenty five gives twenty days

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15 days: Fifteen days would need about thirty three tablets a day

C — 25 days: Twenty five days would need a use of twenty tablets a day

D — 50 days: Fifty days would need a use of ten tablets a day

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Comparing the stock on hand with the daily consumption tells the nurse when to indent, so that the treatment is never interrupted for want of tablets

question: A child weighing 60 kilograms is prescribed 5 milligrams per kilogram per day of a drug in two divided doses. Each dose is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 150 milligrams

🧠 Method: The total daily dose is 60 multiplied by 5, which is 300 milligrams, and half of it, that is 150 milligrams, is given at a time

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 300 milligrams: Three hundred milligrams is the whole day's dose and not a single dose

C — 75 milligrams: Seventy five milligrams is one quarter of the daily dose

D — 600 milligrams: Six hundred milligrams is double the daily dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Paediatric doses worked out from the weight are always checked by a second person before they are given, since a decimal error can be ten times too large

question: An intravenous infusion of 500 millilitres is to run over 4 hours through a set that delivers 20 drops per millilitre. The drip rate per minute is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 42 drops

🧠 Method: Five hundred multiplied by twenty gives ten thousand drops, and dividing by two hundred and forty minutes gives about forty two drops a minute

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20 drops: Twenty drops a minute would take over eight hours

B — 25 drops: Twenty five drops a minute would run the bottle in nearly seven hours

D — 60 drops: Sixty drops a minute would finish the bottle in less than three hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The rate is counted for a full minute with a watch at the start and rechecked at intervals, since the rate changes as the arm moves or the cannula shifts

question: How much glucose is present in 1000 millilitres of a 5 percent glucose solution?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 50 grams

🧠 Method: Five percent of one thousand millilitres is fifty millilitres, and since a five percent solution contains five grams in each hundred millilitres, the total glucose is fifty grams

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 500 grams: Five hundred grams is far more than a bottle can hold in solution

B — 100 grams: One hundred grams would be a ten percent solution

D — 5 grams: Five grams is the amount in one hundred millilitres

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: The energy value of these fifty grams is about two hundred kilocalories, which is why intravenous fluids alone cannot meet a patient's nutritional needs

question: A health worker walks 10 kilometres towards the north, then 10 kilometres towards the east and then 10 kilometres towards the south. She is now:
solution:

question: All patients in a ward have fever. Some patients with fever are dehydrated. Does it follow that some patients in the ward are dehydrated?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. no, it does not follow

🧠 Method: The dehydrated patients with fever may all be from outside the ward, so the conclusion does not necessarily follow

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

💎 PNC Trick: Distinguishing what certainly follows from what is merely possible is the same discipline needed when one finding is used to support a clinical conclusion

question: In a class of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 29th

🧠 Method: The rank from the bottom is forty minus twelve plus one, which is twenty ninth

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 30th: Thirty would mean that he is eleventh from the top

C — 28th: Twenty eight would leave out Ravi himself

D — 27th: Twenty seven would correspond to a rank of fourteen from the top

💎 PNC Trick: Adding one after subtracting avoids the mistake of counting Ravi twice or missing him altogether

question: A rectangular hall is 12 metres long and 8 metres wide. The number of square tiles of side 2 metres needed to cover the floor is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 24

🧠 Method: The area of the floor is ninety six square metres and the area of one tile is four square metres, so twenty four tiles are needed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

💎 PNC Trick: Working first with the areas and then dividing gives the right number, whereas dividing the length and the width separately often leads to an error
